entity_title: Register your Berlin address within 14 days
fact_text: Even as an EU national with full free movement, you must register your new main residence at a Berlin Buergeramt within 14 days of moving in. This Anmeldung is the legal trigger for your tax ID, payroll and most contracts, so book the appointment before you arrive.
evidence_quote: Wenn Sie eine Wohnung als alleinige Wohnung oder Hauptwohnung in Berlin bezogen haben, müssen Sie sich innerhalb von 14 Tagen nach Ihrem Einzug anmelden.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed that free movement means no paperwork for EU citizens. Actually every resident must complete the municipal Anmeldung within 14 days of moving in. Action: book a Buergeramt appointment as early as possible - Berlin slots are scarce.

entity_title: A lease is not enough - get the landlord confirmation
fact_text: To register you must present a Wohnungsgeberbestaetigung, a signed move-in confirmation from your landlord. Your rental contract does not substitute for it, and without it the Buergeramt will refuse the Anmeldung.
evidence_quote: Die Vorlage eines Mietvertrages ersetzt nicht die Wohnungsgeberbestätigung.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the signed lease proves your address for registration. Actually you need a separate signed landlord move-in confirmation (Wohnungsgeberbestaetigung); the lease does not replace it. Action: ask the landlord for the signed Wohnungsgeberbestaetigung on the day you get the keys.

entity_title: Keep the Meldebestaetigung - it unlocks everything
fact_text: When you register in person the Buergeramt hands you the Meldebestaetigung on the spot. This registration confirmation is the document banks, employers and the tax office rely on, so keep several copies.
evidence_quote: Nach Prüfung der Unterlagen erhalten Sie sofort die Meldebestätigung.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed EU citizens in Germany receive a residence permit or card. Actually there is no permit - the address Meldebestaetigung from the Anmeldung is what proves your registered residence and unlocks bank accounts and payroll. Action: keep the Meldebestaetigung safe; you will be asked for it repeatedly.

entity_title: No residence permit needed - you already have the right
fact_text: As a French (EU) national you have an automatic right to live in Germany and cannot be required to hold a residence permit; in your first three months no residence document at all can be demanded. The only registration you owe is the municipal address Anmeldung.
evidence_quote: During the first 3 months of your stay in your new country, as EU national, you cannot be required to apply for a residence document confirming your right to live there - although in some countries you may have to report your presence upon arrival.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed an EU national needs a German residence permit or visa. Actually free movement gives an automatic right to reside and no residence document can be required in the first 3 months. Action: do not apply for any immigration permit - just complete the address Anmeldung.

entity_title: Your non-EU spouse gets derived free-movement rights
fact_text: If your spouse or children are non-EU nationals, EU free-movement rules let them join you in Germany under a facilitated procedure and obtain a residence card - not a standard national work or family visa. Their right is derived from your EU status.
evidence_quote: If you are married or in a registered partnership with an EU citizen that is living, working, studying or looking for a job in an EU country different from the one they come from, EU rules make it easier for you to join them there.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a non-EU spouse of a French employee must obtain a full German work or family visa. Actually they hold derived free-movement rights and apply for a residence card under EU rules. Action: use the EU family-member route, not the standard third-country visa process.

entity_title: Your tax ID (Steuer-ID) arrives only by post
fact_text: The 11-digit tax identification number (Steueridentifikationsnummer) is issued to your registered address and, for data-protection reasons, can only be sent by mail - you cannot pick it up or get it instantly. This is why you must complete the Anmeldung first and allow time for the letter.
evidence_quote: Please understand that the IdNo can only be communicated to you through the mail for data protection reasons.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you can request your Steuer-ID on demand at an office. Actually it is only mailed to your registered address, so it follows the Anmeldung and takes some days. Action: register early and give the ID to payroll as soon as the letter arrives to avoid emergency tax withholding.

entity_title: Keep your French driving licence - no swap needed
fact_text: A French (EU) driving licence stays valid in Germany; you do not normally have to exchange it for a German one. Exchange becomes obligatory only in specific cases such as loss, damage, or a traffic offence committed in Germany.
evidence_quote: If you move to another EU country, you don't usually have to exchange your driving licence for a local one.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you must convert to a German licence soon after moving. Actually EU licences remain valid and exchange is voluntary except in defined cases. Action: keep driving on your French licence; exchange only if it is lost, damaged, or you commit an offence.

entity_title: No work permit - you can start work immediately
fact_text: As an EU national you may take up employment or self-employment in Germany without any work permit, and you need not wait for any registration before starting. The headline reality of this corridor is free movement, not immigration clearance.
evidence_quote: As an EU national, you're entitled to work — for an employer or as a self-employed person — in any EU country without needing a work permit.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed HR must secure a work permit or Blue Card for a French hire in Germany. Actually EU nationals need no permit and may start immediately. Action: skip immigration sponsorship and focus onboarding on Anmeldung, tax ID and health insurance.

entity_title: No tax ID on file means emergency tax class VI
fact_text: If you cannot give your employer your Steuer-ID, the law (Section 39c Income Tax Act) requires them to withhold wage tax at tax class VI - the highest rate, with no allowances. Overpaid tax is refunded later, but the first payslips can be sharply reduced until the ID is supplied.
evidence_quote: Solange der Arbeitnehmer dem Arbeitgeber zum Zweck des Abrufs der elektronischen Lohnsteuerabzugsmerkmale (§ 39e Absatz 4 Satz 1) die ihm zugeteilte Identifikationsnummer sowie den Tag der Geburt schuldhaft nicht mitteilt oder das Bundeszentralamt für Steuern die Mitteilung elektronischer Lohnsteuerabzugsmerkmale ablehnt, hat der Arbeitgeber die Lohnsteuer nach Steuerklasse VI zu ermitteln.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed your correct tax class applies from day one. Actually without your Steuer-ID the employer must apply tax class VI (maximum withholding). Action: complete the Anmeldung fast so the tax ID and your ELStAM tax class reach payroll before the first run.

entity_title: Health insurance is compulsory for everyone
fact_text: Health insurance is legally mandatory for everyone living in Germany. As an employee you are normally enrolled in statutory health insurance (gesetzliche Krankenversicherung) with contributions deducted from salary, and you must be able to name a fund when you start work.
evidence_quote: In Germany, you are required to take out health insurance.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed your French cover or EHIC is enough once you live and work in Germany. Actually German health insurance is compulsory for residents and employees. Action: choose a statutory Krankenkasse before your start date so payroll can register you.

entity_title: You cannot freely choose private health cover
fact_text: Employees can opt out of statutory into private health insurance only if their salary is above the compulsory-insurance limit (Versicherungspflichtgrenze). Below that threshold statutory cover is mandatory - private is not a free choice.
evidence_quote: Above a certain salary, you can opt for private health insurance. This salary level is called the compulsory insurance limit.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed anyone can pick private insurance for better service. Actually you may go private only above the compulsory-insurance salary limit; otherwise statutory is required. Action: check gross salary against the current limit before assuming private is available.

entity_title: Non-working family covered free under statutory cover
fact_text: Under statutory health insurance a non-working spouse and your children are covered at no extra premium (Familienversicherung). This differs sharply from private insurance, where each family member pays a separate premium.
evidence_quote: For example, if your spouse does not work, you can include them in your statutory health insurance free of additional charge. The same applies for your children.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed every family member needs their own paid policy. Actually statutory insurance covers a non-earning spouse and children for free, while private insurance charges per person. Action: factor free family cover into any statutory-vs-private decision.

entity_title: Local hire means German social security, not French
fact_text: EU rules put you under one country's social security, as a rule the country where the work is performed, so a French employee locally hired in Germany pays into and is covered by the German system. French coverage is kept only under a genuine posting (detachement) with an A1, for a maximum of 24 months.
evidence_quote: Selon les dispositions européennes, le salarié qui se déplace dans l'Union européenne ou en Suisse doit être assujetti à une seule législation de protection sociale, en règle générale celle de l'État où l'emploi est exercé.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a French employee can stay on French social security while working in Berlin. Actually a local hire falls under German social security; only a true posting with an A1 keeps the French regime, up to 24 months. Action: decide posting vs local hire up front - it determines which country's contributions apply.

entity_title: Posted worker? Carry an A1 certificate
fact_text: The A1 portable document proves you remain insured in France while working in Germany as a posted worker. Without it, German authorities can treat the assignment as subject to German contributions.
evidence_quote: Statement of applicable legislation. Useful to prove that you pay social security contributions in another EU country as a posted worker or while working in several countries at the same time.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a posting arrangement is self-evident to German authorities. Actually you must hold an A1 issued by the French institution to prove continued French coverage. Action: apply for the A1 before the assignment starts and keep it available for inspection.

entity_title: French pension years count toward a German pension
fact_text: A German state pension normally requires at least five years of contributions to qualify. Under EU aggregation your French insurance periods are added to your German ones to meet that minimum, and each country later pays the share it owes.
evidence_quote: In Germany, you must have worked for at least 5 years to be entitled to a pension.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a short stint in Germany yields no German pension because of the 5-year minimum. Actually EU rules aggregate your French years to satisfy the German qualifying period. Action: keep records of your French insurance periods for a future pension claim.

entity_title: Kindergeld: recent EU arrivals face a fourth-month condition
fact_text: EU nationals working in Germany are entitled to child benefit (Kindergeld), but for those who moved in since August 2019 the freedom-of-movement conditions (for example being employed) must be met from the fourth month after entry. It is not automatic from day one.
evidence_quote: Ab dem vierten Monat nach Ihrer Einreise müssen die Voraussetzungen des Freizügigkeitsgesetzes erfüllt sein.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed Kindergeld starts immediately for any EU family in Germany. Actually recent EU arrivals must meet freedom-of-movement conditions from the fourth month after entry. Action: apply to the Familienkasse once employment starts and expect eligibility to hinge on meeting those conditions from month four.

entity_title: Bring a U1 so French work counts for unemployment
fact_text: If you later become unemployed in Germany, your earlier French insurance periods count toward German unemployment benefit only if you obtain a U1 document from France. German benefit is otherwise based on German contributions alone.
evidence_quote: Statement of insurance periods to be taken into account when calculating an unemployment benefit.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed prior French employment automatically counts for German unemployment benefit. Actually the German agency needs a U1 certificate to take those periods into account. Action: request a U1 from the French authority when you leave France, before you might need it.
